relationships.subject: Regulatory T cells
relationships.evidence_quote: regulatory T cells (CD4+CD25+), which are capable of secreting large amounts of IL-10, thereby suppressing the function of Th1 T lymphocytes

relationships.subject: Microglia
relationships.evidence_quote: Once activated, microglia further contribute to the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines such as IL-1, IL-6, and TNF-α, thereby maintaining or amplifying pain states.

relationships.subject: NGF
relationships.evidence_quote: Neurons and mast cells contribute by releasing neurotrophic factors such as brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) and nerve growth factor (NGF), further modulating microglial activity and sustaining inflammation.

relationships.subject: Tanezumab
relationships.evidence_quote: Therapeutic inhibition of NGF using monoclonal antibodies, such as tanezumab, has shown promise in experimental models

relationships.subject: IL-35
relationships.evidence_quote: Both interleukins enhance IL-10 production within inflamed environments [64, 65].

key_findings: Review: pain chronification reflects failed resolution; local rather than systemic inflammation (cytokines, CGRP) matters
Th1/Th17 versus Th2/Treg balance and IL-10 determine pain outcomes
